response: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the principle of equality before the law. It states that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This means that all individuals, regardless of their background, status, or circumstances, are entitled to the same legal rights and protections under the law. The State is obligated to ensure that no one is discriminated against or treated unfairly based on their identity, race, religion, caste, sex, or any other characteristic. This article is a fundamental part of the Indian legal framework, ensuring that all citizens are treated equally and have equal access to justice.
